answer: In a hillside haven a courier leaves a sealed hardware module on a walnut bench beside fresh nectar, yet scenery admits no one. Only one street address may bind one key, because deliverable premises in good standing are scarce. Peers send a fresh nonce; the module must return a manufacturer-signed quote, and the courier scan must name that still-unbound address. A failed quote or a reused door forfeits the collateral. Another identity requires another real lease, another attested module, and another full stake, at least linear in the number of fakes and steeper as reputable premises run out.
